utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mustafa Pistoljevic, nicknamed "Dzigara"?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he lived in Bosanski Samac. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he work at the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mustafa Omeranovic?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these people you are mentioning, I don't know whether they were involved with the Red Cross, whether they worked there. I don't know about it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to show this witness document P50 ter, with the assistance of the usher. It was discussed in the direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, do you see the stamp? It's document P50 ter. Do you see the stamp in the bottom right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read here what it says in the Latin alphabet?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If you want me to, I can help you. Shall I read it and then you can follow me?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: "The Red Cross of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the municipality conference of Bosanski Samac." I am right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume that that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And there is the logo of the Red Cross and also the stamp. And then on the other side -- well, it's written in the Latin alphabet. Can you read that? It's on the same stamp, just different alphabet.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you when you say that that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then the writing on the other side of the seal looks like it's in Cyrillic, in the Cyrillic alphabet. But I think that it says the same thing.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp is not very clear, but you probably know what it says on the seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can recognise the letters, and I think it is Cyrillic writing, so I just want you to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I read the Cyrillic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether it was usual before the outbreak of the conflict that all stamps of official institutions have both Cyrillic and Latin alphabets?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just go back for a second. The names that I mentioned that I read out to you, so based on the names and the last names, were they people of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were people of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I no longer need this document.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I say something, please? Is this an old stamp then, before the establishment of the Serbian Municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I may tell you, this is your document, the document from the exchange of the 24th of September. And it's on all documents, because that was the only seal that was exist -- in existence. So even after that period, the Red Cross did not change its status.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am not familiar with this reorganization.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you may return this document. We don't need it any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: May I make an intervention just for the purpose of the transcript? It was recorded that the document was from the exchange of the 24th [as interpreted] of September. Now, I'm not sure whether that's what counsel said, whether he said the 4th and it was translated as the 24th. But perhaps he could clarify just what he means, because I -- I think he meant the 4th. The transcript should talk about the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's the 4th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, we're going back to the topic now of your meeting with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Miroslav Tadic. You mentioned that you saw him in your neighbour's yard.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You met Miroslav Tadic by accident then.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He came by at a favourable moment for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was at your neighbour's house. Do you know that your neighbour's son worked at his cafe as a waiter?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since you said that it was just a coincidental meeting, you don't need to answer, then, this following question. You then mentioned that there was a conversation about a confiscated vehicle, when Mr. Tadic said that this was a normal occurrence in such circumstances. Did Mr. Tadic say that his car also was mobilised by the authorities, it was requisitioned?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember him discussing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you also talked about the possibility that your things might be taken away from you, and you were talking about your safety. Do you remember if Miroslav Tadic offered you that if you feel that something unpleasant might happen to you, that you could go to his house and be with his wife, together with your children, in view of the fact that his wife was home all the time?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him saying anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now we're moving to another topic, and that's your visit to the Red Cross, when you found out that you and your husband were going to be exchanged. You mentioned that Miroslav Tadic told you that you were allowed to take only 200 German marks with you when you went on this exchange.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read a part of your statement now which you gave to the Prosecution. It's a statement of the 6th and 7th of April, 1995. Do you remember giving a statement then?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the last page, when you -- of the statement, when you were describing your arrival to Bosanska Gradiska and when you were waiting, you stated the following. I am reading: "The soldiers there wanted to search us, but the guards didn't allow them to do that." Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I don't know whether it states "guards," but it's actually the people who were accompanying the buses from -- the people from the Red Cross who were accompanying the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Tadic tell you that you might be searched en route and that your money might be taken away?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He didn't say anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand this warning from Mr. Tadic to -- as a friendly warning and that perhaps he wanted you to conceal this money?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that, because during that time, the money that I had left that remained in Bosanski Samac had disappeared. My mother remained in Bosanski Samac after I left. Other families, they also had no means to live on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be shown document D3/3 ter. I apologise, D5/3 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. D5/3 ter, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Have you looked at the list -- have you seen this list before?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, this stamp in the bottom right corner, can you see it? It's a little more legible. Can you read it more easily than the previous one that I showed you? Can you see what it says on the seal?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same stamp, like on the previous document. It's the old stamp, I guess the one that was used, because you probably didn't have another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Lukac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you find whether his name is on the list or not?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's under number 25. The number is not fully legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's in between number 24 and number 26, so it should be number 25; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he in the bus with you? Was he in that exchange with you, if you are able to remember?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point, I can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see on that list the name of your husband?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name -- my husband's name is under number 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he in the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was on the bus with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then he crossed to the other side.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Muhamed Bicic?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see whether he's on the list?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's right behind number 20, under number 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he with you in the bus?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was on the bus with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was -- did he cross to the other side together with you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Stipo Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Alojzije Balogh?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Alojzije Balogh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he on the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he cross with you to the other side?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was at Dragalici, but he remained on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mladen Borbeli?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is he on this list?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's under number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was he with you on the bus?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he cross to the other side together with you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about him. You're probably talking about people who did not cross to the other side. But I don't remember his face specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, that means that there were some people who arrived for the exchange but they refused to cross to the other side. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody ask you whether you wanted to cross to the other side while you were leaving the bus? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. I assumed that this was organised in that way, but I don't remember anybody asking me that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether during the exchange in Dragalici, there were representatives of the International Red Cross, the OSC, or any other officials from European humanitarian organisations?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether there were any such representatives on the place where the exchange took place, but I know that on the bus, en route, in the so-called pink zone, there were some UN vehicles and that there were some soldiers there in blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, do you feel that Miroslav Tadic helped you and your family to be exchanged, that he helped you and your husband? Did you believe that then or do you believe that now, in view of the fact that you knew him and that you addressed him several times before you went to the exchange?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he helped personally, but I know that he did take part in the so-called negotiations regarding the exchange and that in personal contacts, he said -- he was talking about the staff or the command at Pelagicevo, that was -- he mentioned Stevan Todorovic that as being one of the people who were actually holding up the exchange of certain people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But did you have the impression that he was trying to help you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that I did accept that as help, because for me, as far as I'm concerned, that is like recognition of the fact that it was impossible for me to survive on that side. And he helped me in a certain way to get expelled from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the question from the counsel.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I did find a way out of that situation. I saved my life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The last question before the last answer was not picked by the interpreters. If you can check the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of the transcript, we will have to repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This engagement, this effort from Mr. Tadic, did you feel that this was done out of good intentions towards you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he was a member of the Red Cross at the time, I considered that to be a normal thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, any other counsel. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, if there's any danger of us finishing before 6.00, I think we better be informed now because I haven't got the next witness ready to go. I spoke to my colleague, Ms. Reidy, and our best estimate was -- and she spoke to Defence counsel and our best estimate was there was no way we were going to finish with this witness before 6.00, and on that basis I don't have the next witness ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Di Fazio, in these proceedings, it's difficult most of the time to predict at what time the proceedings with a particular witness will come to an end, because although sometimes indications are given as to how long the cross-examination will take, we tend to go over that. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. The witness is on standby, and he's at the end of a telephone line. I've made arrangements for that. He's not just at loose, so to speak. And I can get him here. But if counsel can indicate if they are going to be finished in ten minutes' time, I'd appreciate it so I can leave the courtroom and make arrangements to get him in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. -- which one is cross-examining? Mr. Pisarevic. How long do you think you will need for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I need three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. And Mr. Pantelic, are you going to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Are you going to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How much time do you think you will need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If everything would be, you know, smoothly, without so many objections and, you know, the explanations, then I would say that I can finish until 6.00. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How much time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Until 6.00 this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pantelic, you're very cooperative. Mr. Pisarevic, please go ahead

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Delic. I have only one question for you. But before I actually put it, I wish on behalf of my client, Mr. Simo Zaric, to express our regret for all that you and your family had to endure throughout the events in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The question that I want to put to you relates to the event when you were harassed by one member of the Serbian army, Stojan Blagojevic. When I spoke to my client about this event, he told me that everything happened exactly the way you described it, as far as his encounter with you is concerned. I also found out that my client was informed of the incident by your father-in-law, Hasan Delic. So can you please confirm, if you know, the fact that it was your father-in-law, Hasan Delic, who informed Simo Zaric of this incident and asked him to help you in some way?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Zaric came by that evening, and my father-in-law, Hasan Delic, came together with him because he would often stay the night with me and the children. I don't know whether he found out from my father-in-law on the way to my home or he had found out even earlier, but in any case, I understood that it was not from Miroslav Tadic that he learned about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: We'll come later to what exactly it means. But I wanted you -- to hear from you that he came that evening together with your father-in-law. Does it mean really that Simo Zaric came that evening to your house together with your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But I thought of it as a coincidence, as a pure coincidence. I was expecting my father-in-law to come at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: But if I understood you correctly, you have no way of knowing whether it was a matter of coincidence or agreement between them.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Delic.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I know you have been through some very difficult moments, but you will agree with me that it was the common fate of all the inhabitants of your town during the war.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. I don't think we all had to go through the same things. We all fared more or less badly, but not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, on the 7th and 6th of April, 1995, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also, on the 28th of May, 1998, you gave another statement to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You gave those statements without coercion, of your own free will, against no promises from the Office of the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before 1995, did you give any other statements relating to the events in Samac to the police or any other authorities?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And how about after 1995, except for this 1998 statement? Did you give any more statements to any authorities regarding the events in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You and your family have residence now in one of the countries of Western Europe.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside Bosnia and Herzegovina, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in that country and when you were dealing with the immigration formalities, did you talk about your past in Samac and what your family had to go through?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not necessary. I got out with the help of my friends and -- using my personal contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in order to facilitate these proceedings, I kindly ask your permission that these two statements of this witness would be put in front of her so that we can go through certain portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, can I have your assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have the Serbo-Croat?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And when you were dealing with a particular paragraph, please direct us to the English version paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of my learned friends from the Prosecution, I will go through this B/C/S version, although it is not consistent with the English version, but it will be chronologically, so you can easily follow -- follow the events. Actually, we would speak about events, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So which statement are you starting with?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will start with statement of 6th and 7th April, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: First page of B/C/S version. The -- there is no paging on this statement, but there is ERN number, and the last two digits are 64 in B/C/S version. Accordingly, in English version, it's second page, the last paragraph. And then we can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Delic, to facilitate this procedure, if you don't mind, I will read, and you just listen carefully and confirm if I am reading this correctly and if that was indeed what you said when you gave the statement. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, you signed those two statements. And you were warned by the investigators that the statements may be used in these proceedings and that this represents your truthful statement?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask Mr. Pantelic to clarify whether he has a version of the statement -- the second statement, because he did talk about the two statements, the one from 1998, in front of him with her signature on it, because certainly the version I have and I understand the version was disclosed was an unsigned statement. The first one was signed, but not the second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. We are dealing with first one, the 1995 one. Can we deal with that first. And then if he's going to refer to the other statement, then we'll -- you can raise the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I just want to confirm with you that this B/C/S version of the statement, you mean it has no page numbers and it has no paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The B/C/S version has more pages than English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: No, no. Are there numbered paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. In B/C/S version, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Are there page numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Page numbers, also. But there are ERN numbers. So we can go through the ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: So no page numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No page numbers in my copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour -- well, Mr. Pantelic, perhaps I could just direct your attention to the bottom right-hand corner, and I think you'll see a number 2 at the bottom of the same page. It has your ERN number ending in 64 and -- et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, probably. But due to the fact that there is voluminous material, probably my learned friends during the copies made wrong position of the page. So in my copy, actually, I don't have page numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We can go by the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We can go through ERN number, and then it will be easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that statement, in the one paragraph before last of the page you are looking at, the first -- the last two numbers in the upper right-hand corner are "64." You stated the following: "In the beginning of 1992, there was a referendum about Bosnia staying within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. All the Serbs participated in this referendum, voting for Bosnia to stay in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. A small number of Muslims participated and almost no Croats. The Muslims who took part in the referendum voted for the most part for or in favour of Bosnia staying within Yugoslavia. I think they did so because they believed that was the only way they could survive as a nation." You did state that. Can you confirm?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This atmosphere reigning in Samac from January to April 1992, you will agree with me that it created among the population of Samac a certain feeling of insecurity because national rifts started to occur along ethnic lines, along three ethnic lines, among the constituent nations.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please be so kind as to turn the next page with the last two digits "65." We are reading paragraph 3. "From speaking to my students, I found out that the general situation in the Croat and Serb villages had become rather tense and that the people in those villages started to guard the villages. I learned that some of my students also participated in this. Boys of 18 or slightly older sometimes stayed away from school, missed classes. Other students would tell me that they had been on night shifts as guards. I remember that one of my students, Marko, was absent for this reason." We are moving on to paragraph 4. "The students told me that the situation between the villages was tense and insecure. They told me that their parents did not allow them to go out after dark because of several shooting incidents that had happened in the villages on several occasions. In the villages, the political tension was worse than in the town. Some of the children stopped coming to school altogether. Some classes had to be cancelled. When I asked the parents why the children were not coming, they explained it was for reasons of safety." Mrs. Delic, you stand by this statement, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I described it at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And that was true of all your students: Croats, Muslims, and Serbs equally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned here that the students in question were those who came from villages. I said that I had noticed that the situation in Croat and Serb villages had become rather tense and that -- and then I continued with the explanation that I got from my students who came from these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But we can easily agree, can't we, that there were Muslim and Croat students in Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Muslim students. I know that there were no Muslim villages around Samac and the strict environs of Samac comprises Croat and Serb villages only. But at any rate, it was about these particular students that I spoke in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please be kind enough and listen to my question. I didn't ask you about the structure of the villages. I asked you very clearly whether the Serb and Croat villages also had Muslim families or students. Yes or no, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we are moving to the third paragraph from the bottom on the same page, the middle of that paragraph. "Some students also left the area with their families, who already at this time foresaw the war and decided to go abroad. On the other hand, new pupils arrived. They were refugees who had fled the war in Croatia. Most of them were Serbs from Vukovar." Mrs. Delic, can we agree in view of the fact that you are an educated woman, you're a teacher, that in an atmosphere or war and the threat of war, one of the defence mechanisms of each individual is to protect themselves and their family. And one of the ways to do that also is to leave that territory and to go to a safer place. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not of that opinion, and I stayed in Bosanski Samac until the end, in that situation, because I felt that if I was not connected with the activities of parties of that kind or with legal or illegal groups which created such a situation and such an atmosphere, that I should have nothing to fear and that I could stay in that town. Unfortunately, that is what I thought, and I stayed until the end in that period in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, let's still go back to my question. Can we agree that certain individuals in order to save themselves and their family and in order to leave an uncertain, insecure area decided to go abroad; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this happened, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The second question which arises from this part of your statement is as follows: You confirmed while my colleague was cross-examining you, that there were also some Serb refugees, and you've also said that just now. Do you have any knowledge about the fact that in the period from January to June 1992, several thousand Serbian villagers, people from the surrounding settlements where power was taken over by Croats, left those areas and came to Samac as refugees? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that because in such a large number of people, it would be possible to see that. I was simply describing the situation where children from -- or youth from the villages of Dubica and Novi Grad at the time came to school from Crkvine or from the neighbouring villages from that area, and that is why I talked to them about how and why they ended up being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, if I may assist in this procedure and if I may assist the Trial Chamber, the surrounding villages, Novi Grad, Odzak, Prud, these are all villages in the environs of Samac, populated by, among other, Serbian citizens; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prud was mostly inhabited by Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. As many as there were Croats in Serbian villages. It wasn't possible to make a precise division. It wasn't easy to do that. So I don't know the exact figures, and I wouldn't even go into anything like that. In this particular case, it's probably true that there were Serbs in Croat villages and that there were Croats in Serb villages. But everybody knew more or less what was the majority population of any particular village.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, let's be very clear. I am asking very clear questions. Could you please give me more clear -- clearer answers. The first question is as follows: Were there any Serbian citizens in the region of the village of Dubica?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one moment. I -- the structure of the village of Dubica or any villages near Dubica or its environs is something that I don't know. I just know the pupils who came to school from the village of Dubica. But I didn't really pay any attention to the population structure of any particular village. I didn't consider that to be very important for me to know at that point, for example, what the majority population of any given village was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I asked you to answer with a "yes" or "no." But you are continuing to expand your answer. I am interested, Mrs. Delic, in the minority, the Serb minority in those areas. Were there any Serb pupils in your school who came from that area; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that. There were some villages like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I know that because of them that there were such citizens in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were there any Serb inhabitants in the town of Odzak?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably there were. I assume so. I don't understand why you are asking me. This is something that is probably known on the basis of research or official documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Witness, just answer questions put to you by counsel, because counsel is dealing with the whole indictment in this case, and some of the matters contained in the indictment may appear to be matters which somebody can do some research on. But just answer the questions as put to you by counsel. If the questions are not proper, the Trial Chamber will say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My question was: When you were in Samac, did you notice in the period from January to June that there were Serb refugees, men, children, women, in the town of Samac and the surrounding villages; yes, no, or I don't know? It's simple.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give an example. In my neighbourhood, I know that there was a Serb refugee from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, the neighbouring villages from Samac, do you know whether there were any refugees in Samac or its environs; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about Serb refugees from the region of Gradacac, which is a Muslim area, specifically from the village of Srnice, that Serb refugees from that region -- came to Samac in May and June of 1992; yes or no, or don't know?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear about that at that time. I don't know whether anybody from that village was in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The paragraph before last, on the page that you have in front of you, reads as follows: "In the week between the 6th and 10th of April, our school was closed because of the tense situation in Sarajevo and in our area. It was a decision taken at a meeting between all employees in the school." This is what you stated in 1995; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, would you kindly turn to the page which bears the last two numbers "67." I will read the fourth paragraph from the top. And the first paragraph is just one sentence. So counting from that first paragraph. It begins like this: "On the third day after the attack, I went to visit my mother, who lived near the primary school. My mother told me that she had seen on the 17th of April a group of men in camouflage uniforms, masked with ski caps. They questioned all the people from the building, asking if they had any information about who had set the primary school on fire." That is what you stated in your statement; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We would agree that those people in camouflage uniforms and with the balaclavas on their heads were special units from Serbia who terrorised the people; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But what I'm interested in here is whether it was they who set the school on fire or did somebody else set the school on fire, since they were actually asking for information about who set the school on fire. Could you please clarify that sentence a little bit. Who was it that set the school on fire?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That thought here is expressed in such a way or is grammatically formulated in such a way that you cannot notice anything but the fact that they were making inquiries. So it's just an affirmation of the fact that that is what they did. But there is no further explanation. I don't know if there is a short passage missing here, but in any case, if I need to provide more details regarding this particular piece of information, then they simply went around making inquiries about who was it who set the school on fire, which does not mean that they didn't do it themselves but just that they found a reason to, as you said, abuse the people who were living in that building so that they wouldn't think that it was them who actually did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is an interesting theory. But could you please answer this question: Is it possible that some other groups, armed groups, carried out this act of sabotage and that these members of the special units were looking for those who carried out that action? Is that possible? MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honour, it's inviting the witness to speculate, and I can't understand why the -- Mr. Pantelic simply doesn't ask the witness: Do you know who did it? It's simple and straight forward and to the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I was thinking that maybe it's -- the problem is the language, maybe. Because when we hear "is it possible," then obviously for us we conclude that you're asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honours. I will ask directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Directly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know who set the school on fire?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that act, so I cannot say that I know who set the school on fire. But after the explosion, the first morning after the explosion, and on the third day when I saw what was happening and who actually was in possession of the weapons, it was logical that these people were securing the entrances to the city in that way and that they were the same ones who set the school on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You probably have information that all three ethnic groups armed themselves secretly, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The parties -- there were nationalist parties, and they probably - I can't confirm this - but they probably received weapons. And it's a fact that possession of weapons and the private acquisition of weapons was something that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On all three sides; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Can we look at the paragraph -- one paragraph before last on the same page I am reading: "On both sides of our house, our neighbours were Serbs. One day, one of them told my husband that he heard from relatives in the police that Serbs were looking for him. He was on a list of suspicious persons, because somebody allegedly fired from our house." You stated that in 1995, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that at that time -- and we're talking about your family -- there was an awareness that your husband was possibly a suspect because of this incident which you described. So he could have been a possible suspect from the police authorities.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly which police authorities you mean. This was after the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. By the ministry of the internal affairs of Republika Srpska, the police station which was headed by Stiv Todorovic. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, then it's possible that something like that could have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are moving now to the next paragraph. "That same day, on the 22nd of May, 1992, the new Serb head of the police, Stevan Todorovic, called on the phone and asked for my husband. When my husband answered the phone, he was told to report to the SUP or he would be picked up by the police. My husband went to the SUP immediately. It was about 5 p.m. An hour later, my husband called me on the phone. He told me that he would not come home and that he had to stay at the SUP for a certain period of time." This is what you stated; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that Stevan Todorovic was the chief of the police, we all know that he was a criminal and that he's not a very virtuous man. So please tell us, doesn't that seem logical to you if the police summons somebody, they go to find out what it is all about? Is there anything strange in the fact that, regardless of who is the chief of police, a citizen who is summoned by the police should respond to that summons? You're an educated woman. Doesn't that seem logical to you? Please answer with "yes," or "no."

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot answer with "yes" or "no" after you have yourself stated that we are talking about Stevan Todorovic, who is a criminal. I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. hope that you would agree with me. We're talking about a person who will not stop at anything in order to become a chief of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Theoretically. Let's forget Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He's a very important person at this point. Also for the rest of the events as they will unfold.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The Serbian police summoned your husband because of some problem. Do you think that this is logical, that this is a legal procedure for the police to summon somebody to see whether they had seen anything, if they're a possible witness?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is what I wanted to hear. Could you please turn to the next page? The last two numbers on that page are "68." I will read paragraph 5 on that page of your statement. "I didn't receive any official information regarding the arrest of my husband, but through conversations with Serbs, I heard that one of the reasons could possibly have been the fact that my husband's company financed the purchase of weapons for Muslims and Croats. The first month they told me that his company was officially being checked, audited. They wanted to find out whether my husband had signed some compromising documents on behalf of the Mebos company." That is what you stated.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I had stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, in this situation - and I am quoting your statement - we have a suspicion that shots were fired from your house. And then on the other hand, there is another suspicion that your husband, through certain financial transactions or operations - so this is not proved, it's just a suspicion - that he financed the purchase of weapons for Muslims and Croats. Should official organs, meaning the police, in your opinion have the right in such a situation to call your husband to clarify the situation? Does that sound logical to you?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Let's say that that it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question -- it's paragraph 3, counting from the bottom: "Members of other ethnic groups, including women, were taken away for forced labour. I was not taken away because I fell into the category of women who were relieved from forced labour because of my educational attainment level and the fact that I had two minor children." Are you aware of the fact that women of Serb ethnicity, too, had to perform work obligation during wartime?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you mean forced labour or work obligation?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean the obligation, the work duty.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did. It depends all on what you imply by "work obligation." Was it in the same job that they used to work before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, you have graduated from the university in Sarajevo, department of economics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You must be familiar with the economic concept of wartime economy, economic conditions during wartime. Was it in your curriculum during your studies?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Perfect. Now, will you please tell me, during the war, when normal routes of business and economy are disrupted, when everything is in chaos, is there an obligation for everyone, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or profession, to make an effort, a war effort, to deal with these problems?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never involved in decision-making about such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. Please, I'm asking you only hypothetically.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hypothetically or theoretically, if we are speaking about equal citizens in such a state community, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, then is it in keeping with the economic doctrine and a certain legal system, if you know about this at all, that during the war, the Ministry of Defence, in addition to its normal duties and purview, should organise also the civilian life and work, things like organisation of the economy, wartime turnover, communications, transactions? From what you know, is this a fact? Is the Ministry of Defence during wartime charged with such things as well?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska and other competent ministries regulated the question of work obligation through decrees and by establishing a certain hierarchy from the supreme authorities, the government, to the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the way it was organised under the new conditions which appeared at the time, which came into being and in which I had to live.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Delic. We have finished with your statement from 1995. And I think that perhaps now we could move on to a different part of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please, I would like to registrar to provide us to put on the ELMO Exhibit P40, and P40 ter. It is in fact the order where -- signed by head of the public safety station that it's forbidden for three or more Muslim Croats to gather together in public places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, while the registrar is looking for this document, if I remember correctly your testimony here before this Court, you told us that you had seen posters and announcements placed around town prohibiting assembly of non-Serbs in groups of more than two or three. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You also said you had seen the signature on such orders, and the signature was that of the crisis staff. Is that correct? Will you please answer?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, please look carefully at the title of this document. Legibility is poor. But this document P50 ter, the upper left-hand corner. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Bosnia brigade, Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please read the number and the date.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 990/92. Date: 4th of August, 1992. "In compliance with" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No. You don't need to read that. Will you please read the signature on this decision. Which service? What does it say at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Legibility is not the best. I suppose it says "head of -- "

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what does it say below?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Delic, we will now agree that your memory was not serving you very well when you said that that order was signed by the crisis staff. We now see something completely different? MR. DI FAZIO: I object to that question, and I'd ask the witness not answer it. That's not what the witness has said at all, nor has she confirmed that this particular document is the document that she saw or has attested to you. That has not been established at all. That question has to be asked first before it can be established that her memory is faulty or that she's mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, just one correction. I think in the transcript, line 14, it says "P50" the exhibit is. I think it's P40. MR. DI FAZIO: I think that's so, if Your Honour please. That must be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The exhibit we are dealing with is P40.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: P40 ter and P40. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps if I might also add to my objection another matter, that perhaps the witness's attention could be drawn to the top left-hand portion of the document says "confidential."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So Mrs. Delic, let me remind you of your statement. I can give you a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you can ascertain whether what you stated is correct. Now, Mrs. Delic, in your statement of year 1995 to the OTP, page 69, perhaps 5, counting from the top, you said the following: "The decree banning the assembly of Muslims and Croats, that is, non-Serbs, was published later. This decree said that members of other ethnicities may not assemble in public places and not even on their balconies or verandas." Did you state that to the Office of the Prosecutor in that statement?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you see this document which is now before you? Did you see it in Samac when you were speaking about this ban on assembly?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document and the signature doesn't matter to me at all at the moment. What concerns me is the essence. That's what's important. It's a prohibition of continued normal life within that community. It was an outrage to publish something like this. Whether it was signed by this or that person is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The question hasn't been answered. The question was: Did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say I had seen the same document. Even this copy is not a very good one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you see any other document containing the same ...

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With similar contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So it could have been the same document.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been. I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... She has said that "I can't say I had seen the same document." MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the situation, I would have thought, could have been remedied in such a simple way. The witness has testified to having seen posters around the town with this prohibition. And it says so in the statement. Why can't counsel ask the witness: Is this the document you saw plastered around town? Simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my question, Your Honours. Is this a document that you saw and that you described, simply as that. And I got the answer that "I am not so sure." What else can I do? Maybe I can try in the other way and then -- because it's 6.00, we can finish for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mrs. Delic, you are aware of the ban on assembly of three or more Muslims or Croats in Samac.

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you saw it somewhere around town?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When you look at this document now, is it possible that it is that document that you saw posted around town?

utterances.speaker: SNJEZANA DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is possible is that the contents is the same as the one I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, I'm finished for today. It's 6.00, so we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall -- how much time do you think you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I have several -- just virtually several questions about the order for requisition of witness's personal car, and then another document that I provided -- I gave it to my learned friends from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you think you need an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Less than an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Less than an hour. 20 minutes maximum, 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking this because the Prosecution has to know whether or not to bring another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, half an hour would be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, the next witness who is around -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- how long is he likely to be? MR. DI FAZIO: My assessment is probably about the length of this witness, and I would hope somewhat shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mm-hm. MR. DI FAZIO: Somewhat shorter. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. In view of the fact that the witness is already here, I think it's -- it's better that we go ahead with the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: I think so. They're husband and wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then after that witness -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- then we finalise our problem on Variant A and B. Yes, I think so. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because we are trying to cut down on how long the witnesses remain in The Hague. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll continue tomorrow with the cross-examination of the witness at 14.15 hours. Tomorrow we'll have to stop our proceedings at about 17.45. We would like to use the last 15 minutes for a Status Conference. We want to look at the list of witnesses for the Prosecution, to see how many more Prosecution witnesses we have and also to find out about the facilities for Mr. Milan Simic, how well they are working, so that we can decide on how we are going to use the facilities as from Monday. So we'll adjourn today and continue our proceedings tomorrow at 14.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
